title: three-tier-fallback-battlemap-draft
summary: Working draft: a compact seller-facing battlemap that sequences three fallback tiers (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and gives field sellers quick heuristics, triage steps, and language to keep pilots alive during capacity/latency/cost events. Aim: give SEs a 1-page mental model + 2-slide quick deck to drive pilot resilience conversations.
key_messages: 1) Always start with the smallest change that reduces cost/latency (routing/caching/batching).
2) Fallbacks are policy-first: map to customer SLO priorities (latency vs cost vs data isolation).
3) Three-tier escalation keeps customer app live while you iterate: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private (or compatible model variant).
slides_outline: Slide 1: One-line problem statement + 15s seller opener
Slide 2: Three-tier battlemap visual (arrow flow + example triggers)
Slide 3: Quick scripts & triage checklist (30s read)
Slide 4: Pilot runbook / success criteria and next steps
battle_map:
ASCII map for quick copy into notes:

  [Tier 1 - Redwood Hosted (fastest time-to-value)]
    - Default routing, burstable, public catalog, best for early pilots
    - Fallback triggers: transient queueing spikes, noisy tenancy, model refills
    - Rapid mitigations: prefix caching, reduce max_tokens, smaller model variant, increase concurrency/window settings

  --> if mitigations insufficient or predictable load -> escalate

  [Tier 2 - Dedicated Capacity (reserved pools)]
    - Reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation
    - Fallback triggers: sustained p95 latency > SLO, cost budget pressure but need lower variance
    - Mitigations: autoscale policy adjust, burst caps, route high-priority traffic to dedicated, reroute low-priority to cheaper quantized variant

  --> if regulatory, strict data residency, or customer requires full isolation -> escalate

  [Tier 3 - Private (VPC / on-prem)]
    - Customer-managed networking or on-prem for regulated workloads
    - Use cases: PHI/PII constraints, sovereign cloud, full performance control for peak workloads

  Policy binder: TTL on fallback, auto-fallback windows, canary route for new model versions, and rollback hooks.
quick_scripts: Seller opener (30s): 'We design fallbacks so your app stays up — small config changes first, then reserved capacity, and only when you need full isolation do we move to private.'
Ops handoff send (Slack/Email): 'Pilot: account ACME; observed p95 latency 1.8x baseline at 09:30 PST; executing tier-1 mitigations: caching + model downshift; next check in 20m; contact: SE Priya.'
Canary prompt for SE lab: 'Route 10% traffic to dedicated. Monitor tokens/requests and p95. If p95 improves by >25% keep route, else revert and escalate to Private.'
objection_responses: Objection: 'Why not just go private from day 1?' -> Response: 'Private adds ops + lead time and price; we prefer staged approach so you only pay for isolation when you need it and we prove workloads.'

Objection: 'Won't fallback change output quality?' -> Response: 'We map quality tiers to business-critical traffic — keep golden prompts on highest tier and run lower-risk queries on cheaper paths; we also run evals to quantify any regressions before routing.'
Objection: 'How do we guarantee failover?' -> Response: 'We codify fallback policy in the routing layer with SLAs and automated rollbacks; SEs can set hard/soft SLOs per route.'
metrics_and_claims: Typical pilot: moving low-priority traffic to quantized variant reduces unit cost ~2-4x (varies by model and tokens)
Observed median-hosted p95 under steady traffic: ~120-220ms for short prompts (customer data will vary)
Dedicated pools reduce latency variance by 30-70% depending on concurrency shape (use customer-specific benchmark during pilot)
examples: Support chatbot (SaaS midmarket): started hosted -> during 9am surge p95 spiked x2; quick fix: enable prefix caching + reduce max_tokens = 35% cost drop and p95 back to target; later reserved dedicated for peak windows.
Healthcare pilot (regulated): began hosted PoC, but pilot required HIPAA safeguard; route: hosted dev -> dedicated staging with audit logs -> private VPC for production (onboarded KMS/HSM).
pilot_playbook_steps: 1) Qualify SLOs: ask for p95 target, acceptable cost multiple, and data residency rules.
2) Baseline: run 1k synthetic requests representative of expected 95th percentile; capture tokens, p95, error rates.
3) Tier-1: apply caching/batching/model variants + re-run baseline (30-60 mins).
4) Tier-2: provision dedicated pool for a controlled % of traffic (canary 5-10%). Monitor 1 business day.
5) Tier-3: private deployment planning: timeline, infra, compliance checklist. Estimate TTM and costs.
6) Acceptance: define success criteria (latency, cost per 1k tokens, error tolerances), sign-off for production cutover.
